name: Restoration of string
description: A substring of some string is called the most frequent, if the number of its occurrences is not less than number of occurrences of any other substring. You are given a set of strings. A string (not necessarily from this set) is called good if all elements of the set are the most frequent substrings of this string. Restore the non-empty good string with minimum length. If several such strings exist, restore lexicographically minimum string. If there are no good strings, print " NO " (without quotes). A substring of a string is a contiguous subsequence of letters in the string. For example, " ab ", " c ", " abc " are substrings of string " abc ", while " ac " is not a substring of that string. The number of occurrences of a substring in a string is the number of starting positions in the string where the substring occurs. These occurrences could overlap. String a is lexicographically smaller than string b , if a is a prefix of b , or a has a smaller letter at the first position where a and b differ.
input_specification: The first line contains integer n ( 1 ≤ n ≤ 10 5 ) — the number of strings in the set. Each of the next n lines contains a non-empty string consisting of lowercase English letters. It is guaranteed that the strings are distinct. The total length of the strings doesn't exceed 10 5 .
output_specification: Print the non-empty good string with minimum length. If several good strings exist, print lexicographically minimum among them. Print " NO " (without quotes) if there are no good strings.
approach_summary: Uncover mathematical invariant or parity constraint. Construct the solution step-by-step maintaining the validity condition without exhaustive search.
